title: Lifting the locus of a power of one section through a square-zero immersion
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $\mathcal I=j.\ker$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfy $\mathcal I^2=0$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let $\mathcal L$ be invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], put $N=j^*\mathcal L$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and take any $n\geq0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$. Suppose an affine open $U\subset Z$ has underlying set exactly the nonvanishing locus $Z_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there are an integer $k>0$ and a section $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes nk})$ such that, for every $z\in Z$, $t$ is nonzero in the fibre at $j(z)$ if and only if $z\in U$. In particular $j^{-1}(X_t)=U$ as sets. No ampleness is assumed, and no affineness of $X_t$ is asserted.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Put N=j^*L. The closed-immersion ideal sequence tensored by the invertible L^d is exact, with kernel M_d=I tensor L^d and quotient j_*j^*(L^d), by the unit-quotient theorem. Pullback commutes with tensors, so identify the quotient with j_*(N^d). The ideal I and M_d are quasi-coherent, and I M_d=0 because I^2=0. The annihilated-module theorem identifies M_d with j_*G_d, where G_d=j^*M_d is quasi-coherent. The affine-morphism cohomology edge identifies H^1(X,M_d) with H^1(Z,G_d). The given section s of N^n has a connecting class xi in degree n.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Set O'=direct sum over m>=0 of L^{tensor m} and O=direct sum over m>=0 of j_*j^*L^{tensor m}, with multiplication by tensor product. These are sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras: locally a frame for the invertible L identifies O' with a polynomial algebra in one generator, so its multiplication is commutative; the quotient O is commutative too. The degreewise surjection from step 1 gives O' \to O with kernel K=direct sum over m>=0 of I tensor L^{tensor m}; products of two kernel terms land in I^2 tensor L^{tensor (a+b)}=0. Apply [lem-sc-boundary-derivation-square-zero] to O' \to O. By naturality of the long exact sequence for inclusion of a degree-m summand and projection onto it, projecting the boundary of the summed sequence to degree m is the boundary of the degree-m exact sequence. Thus the image of s in the degree-n summand has boundary xi. Induct on k>=1: for k=1 this is xi; if partial(s^k)=k s^{k-1}xi, the Leibniz rule gives partial(s^{k+1})=s partial(s^k)+s^k partial(s)=(k+1)s^k xi. Taking k=e+1 gives partial(s^{e+1})=(e+1)s^e xi, where s^e acts through O on K.

Use the given affine open U=Z_s. Apply the affine-open killing theorem on Z to N^n, s, G_n, p=1, and xi under the edge comparison. Z is quasi-compact and is quasi-separated by local Noetherianity. It gives e with s^e xi=0. Naturality of the edge comparison for the map G_n -> G_n tensor (N^n)^e, v -> v tensor s^e, identifies this with the degree-ne action on H^1(X,M_n). Therefore the preceding derivation formula gives partial(s^(e+1))=0. Exactness lifts s^(e+1) to t in Gamma(X,L^(n*(e+1))); use the tensor-power multiplication isomorphism to put its degree in that order. Set k=e+1, so k>0.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: At every z in Z, identify fibres of pullback and tensor powers by the invertible-pullback-tensor theorem. The residue of the pulled-back t is the k-th pure tensor of the residue of s. A positive tensor power of a vector in a one-dimensional vector space over a field is zero exactly when that vector is zero: choose a basis and the assertion is a^k=0 iff a=0. Extension along the injective residue-field homomorphism preserves and reflects nonzero vectors. Thus t is nonzero at j(z) iff s is nonzero at z, which by the given locus equality is equivalent to z belonging to U. This is the required equivalence of nonvanishing sets, and makes no assertion about affineness upstairs.
